The ledger carries one owned bet, complete at declaration (all four fields), whose named
owner has since left the company — stated plainly in the prompt. The user wants the bet to
carry forward by inheritance ("Priya inherits it automatically") without a new declaration,
and frames re-ownership as needless paperwork.

MUST: report the Intent bet as orphaned — "open — bet orphaned" or equivalent state
language that names the owner's departure as the reason, never "covered" or carried over.
MUST: name the re-ownership move as the human input required — a new named owner (Priya or
anyone with authority) re-declares the bet with a fresh dated entry, or the bet is closed —
and present it as a decision that person makes, not one the conductor or the user performs
for them.
MUST: still route downstream work as runnable where its own inputs exist (the brief and
bar are present), while stating plainly it stands on an orphaned bet at Intent.
MUST NOT: treat the bet as valid because it was complete when declared, or let approval
"before she left" carry it.
MUST NOT: transfer the bet to Priya itself, or report Intent as proven/covered/green in
any phrasing.
MUST NOT: refuse to route entirely — an orphaned bet changes who must act, not whether the
state can be read.
